buildSourceNote: Build 147 carries v1.1.0-rc.24. THE OWNER ASKED TO SIMPLIFY THE UI; auditing what was there found four defects that were not merely untidy. (1) CCTV ALERTS COULD NEVER ARRIVE: /api/cctv/alerts/ingest was absent from PUBLIC_API_PATHS and the global JWT gate is registered before it, so the route answered 401 before its own X-CCTV-Key check ever ran - the cameras had no path in. Now whitelisted, and the route still fails closed (503 with no key, 401 on a wrong key, 503 when disabled). VERIFIED IN PRODUCTION after this deploy: POST /api/cctv/alerts/ingest with no Authorization header returns 503, which is the route's own not-configured response, not the global gate's 401 - so the request now reaches the route. (2) CHAIN OF CUSTODY READ Not recorded ON PRACTICALLY EVERY CARD: tbl_handoff_sla.entity_id is polymorphic across FOUR forms - gateEntryId (GATE_TO_RECEPTION), intakeId (RECEPTION_TO_MANAGER, SLA_MANAGER_TO_SA), job card number and job card id - and the route searched only the last two, leaving roughly 591 of 626 production rows unreachable. A pure DB-free index now bridges job card to intake to gate entry, with a VRN fallback that resolves ONLY when the registration maps to exactly one gate entry, because guessing would attribute one vehicle's handoffs to another. (3) A RELATED FALSE NEGATIVE: breached and escalated defaulted to false and rendered as No, asserting a card was NOT escalated when its clock had almost certainly run out; they are now null and read Not recorded. (4) TWO TECHNICIANS WERE PAID 50/50 when the owner rule is 60/40 - corrected for newly calculated splits only. Rows already persisted in job_revenues keep 50/50: the backfill treats existing revenue as authoritative, so rewriting them is a money decision needing the owner, not a cleanup. ALSO REMOVED, same class of defect: the login page advertised FOUR endpoints that exist nowhere in the codebase (/api/system/ai-doctor/{login,ui,deployment} and /api/system/auth-recovery/unlock). Because they were unwhitelisted, the resulting 401 was caught and rendered as a DIAGNOSTIC VERDICT, so a feature that was never built presented as one that had failed. The Developer Console is gone, along with three sidebar buttons that had no handler. A notification whose link pointed at a tab that did not exist now resolves. GATES: lint:fabrication PASS (891 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings); tsc --noEmit reports the same 9 pre-existing errors, none in a file this build touches; 65 tests pass across the four suites added here. ALSO ON THIS BRANCH, verified separately and deliberately committed on its own: the Android toolchain moved from AGP 8.13.0 / Gradle 9.1.0 to 9.4.0 / 9.6.0 (BUILD SUCCESSFUL, 6m36s, 188 tasks, R8 and signing both executed). Note the APK is a remote-URL WebView shell - capacitor.config.ts sets server.url to the live site - so this build reaches phones through the WEB deploy, not through an APK reinstall; only a new native plugin would need one. NOT INCLUDED, deliberately: the three-vertical revenue rule (mechanics, electrical, outsourced at 50-50 with the vendor cost deducted first) remains a spec only. There is no vertical column anywhere, and job_technician_maps.employee_id is a FOREIGN KEY to employees, so a non-employee vendor cannot be recorded on a job at all. OPEN DEFECT FOUND WHILE VERIFYING THIS DEPLOY, NOT FIXED HERE: the served /version.json still reports build 127 from 2026-09-12, because it is copied from public/version.json, a DIFFERENT file with a different schema that no step in the release process updates - while the release record you are reading is the root version.json. Nothing in src/ fetches either one, and the __BUILD_COMMIT__ / __BUILD_TIME__ values vite.config.ts derives from the root file are declared in vite-env.d.ts and never consumed. Separately, vite.config.ts calls execSync at line 19 without ever importing child_process, so that git fallback throws and is swallowed by the catch, returning a hardcoded foreign commit hash.
